elysiumalmanac.why.a_bad_bargain: A quarter of an FE a tick for every rpm, nothing below 32, and it draws 10 torque. Across to FE and back through a motor, half the power comes home. The next age does it properly.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_bag_that_helps: A lens picks things up off the ground. A ration tin feeds you when all of a food is wanted, never a steak for one point. A restocker tops up the stack in your hand every half second.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_band_on_the_road: Every two to four minutes a band of two or more turns up 24 to 40 blocks out, never more than six within 64. That is the world, not your standing: the roads are simply not safe.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_bedroom: Wardrobe, drawers, nightstand, desk. Then rugs, runners, cushions and pillows below and curtains, drapes and canopies above, in the game's own wool, so sixteen colours cost no new texture.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_better_lump: Coal in, coke out 900 ticks later; a log to charcoal in 600. Coke burns 3,200 ticks, twice coal. No hopper can feed an oven, so build three and visit them.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_busy_assembler: 96 FE on the low wire and 40 ticks a run: slower than your own hands, because what it sells is not having to be there. Starved of power it is slow, and never stopped.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_cage_that_never_sle: Indifference sets the watching range to 256 blocks, past which nothing ticks anyway. Twelve steps is the most haste a spawner takes, and all twelve cost seventy-eight runes.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_cell_like_a_wire: Sixteen times again: 268 million FE, and it moves 16,384 a tick, exactly the ceiling on any connection. A cell that pushed more than that would only burn its own wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_chest_joins: Placed on a chest, a barrel or anything with slots, it makes that inventory part of the network. It costs two devices' worth of draw and asks nothing of what it exposes.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_companion: Eleven creatures that each do a block's job, a light or a reach or a bite, and a wild one is only in the way. Wheat seeds tame the next. Every gift fades within ten seconds of stopping.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_court: A court reads as a sentence: a head, a herald calling the rest, a swarm, a shield, something at range. Kill the herald first. The rot and pack heads stand on the first rung at 39 health.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_crate_of_parts: Twenty-seven slots and two fittings, and the same parts as a bag. The jars this replaces had one upgrade system for what you wear and another for what you put down.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_door_of_stone: The game has eleven wooden doors and one of iron. This is a door of stone, and like the iron one it wants redstone rather than a hand.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_face_to_take_from: A hopper under an interface takes from the network as if it were a chest, so a furnace can feed straight out of your drawers. Two devices of draw.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_factory_cell: Steel and gold plate round a basic cell: sixteen times the room and eight times the throughput, 16.7 million FE and 2,048 a tick. What a factory runs on overnight.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_hall_of_three: A hollow box of casing, three to seven on a side, the port in one wall and rods inside. Prod the port: it names the size, rods, channels and safe throttle, or the nearest wrong block.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_high_wire: Steel carries 4,096 and loses a tenth of a per cent a block. Everything the Ascent builds wants it, and none of it will talk to a gold line without a transformer between.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_kitchen: The one room the game gives you nothing for. A counter, a sink and a stove in any of thirty-three materials, a table to eat at, and a planter or a trough for the window.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_legend_sigil: Gold, lapis and a diamond make the one template every named weapon is smithed with; the weapon underneath decides which comes out. Whisperfang is an iron sabre and an amethyst shard.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_mailbox: A tag is paper and a sign; claiming an address costs three levels, because a name is the scarce thing in a post. A letter is one paper of postage and takes 600 to 6000 ticks to arrive.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_medium_wire: Gold carries 1,024 before it burns and loses half what copper does. Copper touching gold does not join at all: two voltages refuse each other, and only a transformer bridges them.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_myth: Eight myths, one bane each and one answer: a carved pumpkin against the glasseye's stare, a golden apple for the siphon's drain, a shield for the swarmhand's numbers. More armour is never it.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_netherite_brush: Four ticks a stage and five blocks of reach: the fastest a brush is allowed to be, and still slower than breaking the block, which is the band the whole mechanic lives in.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_patient_boiler: With nothing on the grid asking, a turbine burns nothing and keeps its coal. It lights on demand and makes 120 FE a tick on the low wire, and not one more.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_place_to_sleep: A bag is for the night and a hammock for the day, and neither moves where you wake after dying. Exactly one of the two works at any tick. A hammock hangs from rope and nail.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_porch: Six chime materials, six notes: no wind below y 48, full wind at 192, and two sounds a second at most within eight blocks. A fire pit is light 11 for four sticks and a coal; the mat gives none.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_potion_charm: Craft it with a potion to fill it. Worn, it keeps the effect up 12 seconds at a time and spends a point of its 512 only when it does. Nothing instant, nothing harmful, refilled the same way.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_reason_to_choose: Reach, and nothing else at all. You will hit things before they hit you, and you will be very sorry the first time one gets inside it.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_ring: Two ring slots. An aetherium band lands blows 15 per cent harder from level 10, a bloodlet ring takes back 6 per cent of what you deal. Made ones ascend without a ceiling; found ones never do.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_road: Paving is worth most to whatever is slowest, which is the opposite of what you would guess and is the reason a cart on a road beats a hauler off one.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_roof_that_closes: Two pitches, each with a slope, an outer corner, an inner corner and a ridge, or an L-shaped house could not be closed. Then a sill, an awning and a cornice, which make an elevation look done.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_rune_on_it: Obsidian and one thing: sugar for haste, slime for swarming, iron bars for crowding, an ender eye for vigilance, gunpowder for scattering. Each step costs one more rune than the last.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_satchel: Nine slots and one fitting. Use it to open it; crouch and use it with a part in the other hand to fit one; with the other hand empty, the last part comes back out.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_scythe: It takes a crop and puts one seed straight back in the ground; you keep none of those seeds and all of everything else, so a scythe is a harvest and never a seed farm.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_slot_is_a_question: Three found trinkets and room for only some of them. Every one costs something or only works sometimes, because a trinket strictly better than an empty slot is not a decision.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_starved_machine: Prod a machine for its share and what it holds. At half a share it runs at half speed and never stops. Crusher 64 FE, rolling mill 96, separator 256, arc furnace 512.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_wall_that_joins: Fences of stone, with a gate in them. They reach for each other and not for the oak fence next door, which is the whole difficulty with fences.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_warded_thing: Thirteen creatures and six wards: flame, shot, blast, rot, frost, curse. The right protection leaves between 35 and 80 per cent of the fight, and no one ward answers more than three.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_warehouse_wall: Sixteen steel drawers, four kinds and 8,192 of each: over half a million items behind one controller that answers a hopper as though it were a single chest.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_way_up: The game has one ladder and it is oak. These come in thirty-three materials, rope in eleven, and a trellis climbs too: drop down a column of any of them and you land without a scratch.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_whole_skeleton: Ocelot keeps creepers off, wolf skeletons; chicken softens a landing, guardian lets you breathe, creeper blunts a blast; sheep regrow wool, villagers restock. Seven, none a better other.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_wider_hold: Radius nought to two: up to 25 chunks, for 30 torque at 240 rpm. The cost per chunk is the same at every width, and gearing moves power about without making any, so it cannot cheat.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_window: Panes in anything at all, which the game does not have: it has glass and it has iron bars, and nothing between them in any material you like.
elysiumalmanac.why.accelerate: A pot alone is 1.5 times the ground. Fed a full share of 48 FE on the low grid, the pot beside it runs four times that. With no pot to hurry it draws nothing at all.
elysiumalmanac.why.accelerator: A room of pots works on torches. A room that keeps up with a factory needs a factory.
elysiumalmanac.why.across_the_back: Thornplate returns a tenth of every blow to whoever struck it. The ashen mantle burns back a third while you burn, and quiet hours moves both meters at half speed.
elysiumalmanac.why.again_and_again: Double is 81, triple 729, quadruple 6,561. Each tier is framed in a block the game already has, copper first and quartz last, so a wall of them reads its own depth.
elysiumalmanac.why.alloys_of_alloys: Signal alloy is electrum and two redstone; hardened bronze two bronze and an invar. With stainless these are the second tier, where a furnace stops being enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.altar: Four pedestals two blocks out, relays four out, and the whole thing lies flat: a pedestal one block up is one the harness never looked at. Nothing ticks until you use it.
elysiumalmanac.why.alternator: Rotation in, power out, six times what a dynamo manages. It draws more torque than one water wheel can push.
elysiumalmanac.why.an_unidentified_lump: Nine artifact shards make one. Identifying it is a roll and not a choice, because a choice would mean one artifact and two that live in a wiki. Each of the three is equally likely.
elysiumalmanac.why.an_unstable_one: Structures place unstable spawners and they say so on the outside. Take a pickaxe to one and it goes off at power 3, a creeper and a half: enough to hurt you, not enough for the room.
elysiumalmanac.why.apiary: Break a hive and the bees fall out as items; an apiary takes sixteen of them and two upgrades. A bare hive runs at a fifth of the ceiling, and the ladder earns the rest back.
elysiumalmanac.why.aquaponics: Two seeds in, two wheat out for 600 FE, and a cod in the side tray for every four crops. It wants light 9 from anywhere, not sky, so a lit cellar will do; the bioreactor cannot say that.
elysiumalmanac.why.arc_furnace: 512 FE a tick, which is twice what a copper wire will carry. This is the machine that teaches you voltage.
elysiumalmanac.why.ascendant_essence: The fifth rung, and the only thing on it is netherite. Sixteen times the wait of a coal seed, and the build still checks that a mine of it wins.
elysiumalmanac.why.ask_the_line: Any shaft reports the whole line: its speed, and an effort from nought at freewheel to one at stall. A machine that is too slow says so: needs 8, turning at 6.7. Timber shears above 64.
elysiumalmanac.why.ask_the_spawner: Look at a spawner and type /spawner: five axes with the steps spent and the numbers they bought, then the behaviours that are on. It needs no permission, because all it does is read.
elysiumalmanac.why.assembler: The core plans and builds nothing. Four assemblers is four jobs at once; sixteen is as many as one core will run, and every one of them is a machine on the grid.
elysiumalmanac.why.assembly_core: It reads every recipe the game has loaded, works out what a request would take, and tells you before it touches a single item in your drawers.
elysiumalmanac.why.at_the_shoulder: Four things that hover: a mote lights the dark for you and for everything looking for you, a carrion drone picks over your kills, a purge drone bleeds the null field out of you at a price.
elysiumalmanac.why.at_the_throat: A voidglass pendant raises psionic potency a fifth; a warden's gorget makes willpower shields a quarter larger. The empty reliquary: a shield twice the size over a body half as quick to mend.
elysiumalmanac.why.at_the_waist: A dimensional anchor ignores the first 3 blocks of any fall, a kinetic spur avoids one blow in twenty, a plasma cord mends 30 per cent faster. The gravebound coil makes falls harmless, and is noticed.
elysiumalmanac.why.auto_trader: The auto trader takes a trade every ten seconds from what it is fed and puts the result out the other side. The viewer looks at the villager in it once a second and does nothing else.
elysiumalmanac.why.awakened_seed: Twice the yield per plot, and the farm is held to the same share as before, so awakening buys you half the room and none of the income. Thirty-one recipes, one for every seed.
elysiumalmanac.why.bait: Eleven families of water, a bait for each. Bait pulls the table four times towards its own family and removes nothing. A rod carries sixty-four and every catch eats one.
elysiumalmanac.why.balconies_and_bridges: A balcony without a railing is a hole; a bridge is deck, rail and support or it is not a bridge. Quoins turn a corner; banisters, catwalks and girders reach the one beside them like a fence.
elysiumalmanac.why.beds: Soil gets faster as it gets dearer. A clay bed runs at 1.35 and takes crops and kelp; a gravel bed grows the hardy and the aquatic; an ashen bed at 1.55 is where nether wart goes.
elysiumalmanac.why.bigger_bags: Knapsack 18, haversack 27, rucksack 36, expedition pack 45, one more fitting at each step. A bag may not go inside a bag: capacity would be a recursion with no bottom to it.
elysiumalmanac.why.bigger_station: Medium takes 150 of each, big 200. Each is built round the smaller from the same corner, so the upgrade rebuilds the station in place and covers the old one completely.
elysiumalmanac.why.bind_two: A jump is 2,000 plus up to 18,000 for distance, half of that by 4,000 blocks, or 20,000 to another world. A stone holds 64,000, trickles 2 a tick alone and 64 on a wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.bioreactor: Water, sky and 12 FE a tick, and every 400 ticks a briquette that burns 1600, as coal does. Burn it in a kiln: clay and glass in 160 ticks, not 200, on half the fuel or 3 FE a tick.
elysiumalmanac.why.black_water: Oil lies in lakes in the deserts of home and on Cinderveil and Frostfall. A lake is not a supply; an oil finder, a stick with steel and redstone on it, says what the ground under you holds.
elysiumalmanac.why.bloom: Glow lichen set in honeycomb is bloom resin, two at a time. In glass it is lit from inside and never warm; in a brass frame it is a lantern, two to a craft. Neither burns a thing.
elysiumalmanac.why.board: No fire at all. Beef to two minced, cabbage to three leaves, wheat to dough, a milk bucket to cream and butter; the sandwiches take 200 ticks here. Start it with an empty hand.
elysiumalmanac.why.bobbers: The wait is 100 to 600 ticks. Cork takes a quarter off it; glow makes the night fish bite by day; lead fishes one band deeper than the water says; lantern does the last two at once.
elysiumalmanac.why.bones_of_a_wall: Pillars, beams and posts make a wall look built; lattices, shutters and screens divide a room. Panelling stands a sixteenth off the wall, blinds three, boards five, and a frame is proved hollow.
elysiumalmanac.why.botany_pot: Sixty-one materials, three fittings, one mechanism: a soil in the bottom slot, a sprout on top, light 9 above it or nothing grows. A carrot in farmland comes up in 640 ticks.
elysiumalmanac.why.both_sides_have_an_op: Fifty, from both sides. Every kill moves Favor and Suspicion through the faction rules, and standing dispatches send lictors and reavers after whoever has earned them.
elysiumalmanac.why.bottle_fuel: A glass bottle used on the refinery takes 250 mB as a canister. A bucket is a thousand and goes into a rocket just as well; the canister also goes into a jet suit, which a bucket does not.
elysiumalmanac.why.boulders: Stone, mossy and basalt boulders sit where the land wants them, and patches of bloom, scrub and thicket fill the ground between. A landmark is anything you can see from a long way off.
elysiumalmanac.why.brass_bands: Copper round a timber drawer and a gold nugget under it: two kinds, sixty-four stacks of each. A timber drawer holds 2,048 of one thing; this holds 4,096 of two.
elysiumalmanac.why.brass_shaft: Timber shears above 64 rpm. Brass takes 192, and nothing in the second age will run on less.
elysiumalmanac.why.breed: A jar of stone and a jar of meadow in one hive, then a treat, and the hive holds their child. Iron is the first of ninety-two bred species, every one priced under a quarter of a mine.
elysiumalmanac.why.breeder: Twelve food to a child every minute, a child to an adult in two, a cure in 3000 ticks where a hand takes 2400. Every station is slower than you; what it buys is attention, not speed.
elysiumalmanac.why.brick_kiln: Twenty-five coke bricks round one hollow block, the oven at the middle of a face. No wire and no fuel: its cost is time and somewhere to put it, which is what a kiln is.
elysiumalmanac.why.bright_essence: Every rung is twice as slow as the one below, so a farm loses to a mine until it is a deliberate project. Second rung: nickel, silver, aluminium, lithium, lapis, quartz, glowstone.
elysiumalmanac.why.broad_tool: Clears a three-by-three, costs a point of durability for every block of it, and swings slower than the pickaxe it is standing in for. All three of those are on purpose.
elysiumalmanac.why.bronze: Three copper and a tin. The first alloy, and the first time the chain has a step in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.brush_a_site: Suspicious dirt, red sand, fossiliferous dirt. What a site holds is decided by where it is, so a site brushed halfway still holds it tomorrow, and breaking and replacing one rolls nothing new.
elysiumalmanac.why.built_for_the_room: Each is built on spawn for the average level of players within 64 blocks, then fixed. Health grows on a square root and damage nearly in a line, so a fight gets deadlier, not longer.
elysiumalmanac.why.burn_for_it: Coal, charcoal, a blaze rod or a coal block: it burns what a furnace burns and drives a line at up to 64 rpm with 24 of torque. The first source that spends something while it runs.
elysiumalmanac.why.cane: Four bamboo woven make two cane for 280 FE, where a grid makes one. Cane blocks, a lattice that keeps sun off and not air, moss on cane for a living wall, and a planter for anywhere flat.
elysiumalmanac.why.capstan: Nothing extra at y 64 and everything at 192, where it makes 14 a tick with four sides open. Wall one side in and you lose a quarter. Worse than a condenser at noon, better at midnight.
elysiumalmanac.why.capturing: An enchantment that turns a kill into a spawn egg: one in eight at the first level, one in five at the second, one in four at the third. Never certain, because a sure egg ends the question.
elysiumalmanac.why.carried: Ten things carried: sigils that raise Favor a quarter or cut Suspicion, a prospect charm that rolls Elysium drops again, and a long memory that holds both meters exactly where you left them.
elysiumalmanac.why.carry_a_cage: Mined with silk touch, the game's spawner drops this one holding exactly what it held, its creature turning in the cage. That is the only moment anybody cared which block it was.
elysiumalmanac.why.cart: It runs on anything that burns, carries nine stacks and loses to walking over rough ground — which is the whole reason you laid the road first.
elysiumalmanac.why.casing: A tier four machine runs on the top wire in the game. You have reached the end of the material chain.
elysiumalmanac.why.catch: A hundred and five fish, and every one is proved to come up somewhere. Where you stand picks the water: fresh or salt, four depth bands, day or night. They swim where they bite.
elysiumalmanac.why.cell: Every grid until now spent what it made the tick it made it. A cell is the first time surplus is worth having.
elysiumalmanac.why.centrifuge: The hungriest machine in the age, and the only route to reactor fuel.
elysiumalmanac.why.change_one_thing: 1,024 FE on the high wire: redstone to glowstone in 260 ticks, charcoal to coal, clay to slime, flesh to leather. The centrifuge, meanwhile, spins soul sand into gunpowder.
elysiumalmanac.why.channels_by_colour: Copper plate round packed ice makes four; a channel and a dye make a dyed one. Channels join when either is plain or both share a dye, so two reactors' plumbing can touch.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.ascent: Power you can keep, and the first thing that can kill you.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.automation: The warehouse stops being somewhere you look things up and starts being somewhere you ask for them.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.first_light: Rotation, and nothing that needs power at all.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.foundry: Alloys, and the top of the material chain.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.reconstructio: Steel, wire, and the first grid.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_bands: The Unsworn and the Empire, in squads on the road, and the two things each side sends when it means it.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_cages: A spawner you can pick up, carry home and tune, one rune dearer each time.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_charms: Eight kinds of slot and forty-five things to wear in them, most of which cost you something.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_commons: Sun, wind and rain on a wire, and a grid that decides what stops first.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_court: The half of the Empire you can talk to, and six trades a village did not have.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_dark: Something to hit things with, and the things.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_dig: Brushes, bones and a lump that might be anything: the slow way to the few things nothing else gives.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_empire: Two meters, three ores, nine runes and a great deal of gear, and a Code that is counting everything you dig up.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_forge: Gear assembled from parts, each part from a material, the whole worked out from what went in.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_geodes: Crystals that grow out of a wall, relics cut from them, and a machine that turns things into other things.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_grove: String and charcoal are the two things nobody farms. Two crops and a tree, so that they are.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_homestead: Somewhere worth coming back to, and what happens if you do not.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_ledger: Who you are, as the Empire has you written down: an origin, a calling, a level, and the web of what you chose to become.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_rift: A door to a dungeon that is never the same twice, and is finished for good once you leave it.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_seams: Every metal in every stone, and why the deeper world pays better for the same vein.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_tomes: Enchanting as a room you build rather than a table you stand at.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_town: Settlements that found themselves, ruins that did not last, and a column eighty blocks high that makes a colony part of something larger.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_wilds: Knowing where anything is, which is most of knowing what to do next.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.warehouse: Somewhere to put all of it.
elysiumalmanac.why.charcoal_block: Nine charcoal to a block and it burns for exactly nine: 21600 ticks, eighteen minutes in one slot. It comes apart into nine again, so a block is storage and not a bargain.
elysiumalmanac.why.charging_draining: It says whether it is charging, draining or holding, and how much of its 1,048,576 FE. A basic cell moves 256 a tick either way, which is exactly what a copper wire carries.
elysiumalmanac.why.cinder_ruins: Catacombs, a crash site, outposts on the lava and one with a dungeon under it, a plaza, a tower and ruins. Two worlds' worth of buildings came here, because the hotter one had no world of its own.
elysiumalmanac.why.cinderlings: Cinderlings are piglins at home, sixteen health and five damage, and do not rot out here. The boars are hoglins with forty health that shrug off most knockback and breed from fungus.
elysiumalmanac.why.cinderveil: 41,000 megametres: 2,134 mB of plain fuel from home. Nine-tenths gravity, air that corrodes, heat that cooks, and water that boils off the moment it is poured.
elysiumalmanac.why.cindrium: Cinder sand and cinder stone, with cindrium, coal, gold, diamond and neptunium below the zero line. Ash storms thicken the corrosion and halve a solar panel; a wall answers both.
elysiumalmanac.why.clad_the_yard: Four ingots make four plates of iron, steel or lunite, and the stonecutter makes slabs, stairs and pillars of them. It looks like a launch site because it is made of one.
elysiumalmanac.why.coal_and_sun: Coal makes 20 FE a tick into a 12,800 buffer and hands 200 a tick to each neighbour. The panel makes 10 by day, nothing by night, and twice that where there is no air to filter the sun.
elysiumalmanac.why.cogwheels: Eight teeth and twenty-four, so three ratios: three to one, one to three, one to one. Each pair reverses the turn and keeps 97 per cent of the power crossing it.
elysiumalmanac.why.colony: Crafted bare; a red or brown mushroom used on it fixes the kind for good. One grows every 4,000 ticks up to three, an empty hand takes them, and a cellar of them reads from the door.
elysiumalmanac.why.comb_centrifuge: What a comb is for: 200 ticks and 24 FE, out come one of the material, two wax and a bottle of honey. A comb of plain honey gives the last two. Nine combs also pack to a block.
elysiumalmanac.why.condenser: Twenty FE a tick at noon, less at dusk and in rain, none at night. It holds 24000 and pushes 200 a tick into what touches it. Brass and glass make six greenhouse frames that let the sky through.
elysiumalmanac.why.conduit: Eight to a craft, and it holds nothing: the generator walks the run, up to 512 conduits and 64 machines. Dye one and it joins only its own colour, so two grids can cross a wall untouched.
elysiumalmanac.why.controller: Every drawer on its bus behaves as one inventory. Point a hopper at it and it finds the right drawer.
elysiumalmanac.why.cooked_and_pressed: An ember plate cooks what goes in, and leaves a pile raw rather than half done if it would not fit. A press screw packs nine into one at compression's own step, so a grid unpacks it.
elysiumalmanac.why.cooking_pot: A campfire under it, four servings out in 400 to 700 ticks. Stock first: bone, onion, carrot. Every soup carries an effect, from comfort to fire resistance.
elysiumalmanac.why.coolant: Four channels. A bare core at full throttle settles at several times meltdown; three channels is not enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.copper_wire: A grid divides what it has: everything on it gets the same share. Copper carries 256 before it burns.
elysiumalmanac.why.cordon_blade: Ten metals from the Cordon, each placed on the ladder by the damage it adds: lunite at the foot with 3 and 1,450 uses, nullsteel at the top with 17 and 5,248. Every shape comes in all ten.
elysiumalmanac.why.count_to_redstone: Show it an item, then crouch and use it to step the count: 1, 16, 64, 256, 1,024, 4,096. It gives a signal once the network holds that many. Stop a farm when the store is full.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_amnesty: Every office that reads Suspicion carries two. One takes 25 off, which is exactly a band, and never below your claim's floor: the Empire forgets your conduct, not your fortress.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_arrival: Every five minutes, one chance in three, one envoy at a time, within 24 blocks. Their ledger is rolled once on arrival, bought from on vanilla's screen, and gone with them in twenty minutes.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_commission: Crouch and use the Emperor or the Queen: eight times a trade's quantity within three days, three top-shelf rolls on settling and twelve standing. Any envoy settles it; lapsing costs eight.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_memory: Crouch empty-handed and a villager says what it remembers of you, worst first: trades, blows, a killing within sixteen blocks. Too upset, or holding too much against you, and it will not deal.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_metal_benches: Eight copper round an iron ingot or a nugget, and a jobless villager takes the job. The gear smith buys copper for tools; the salvager takes rotten flesh and bone and sells chain and TNT.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_offices: The Sentinel deals with anyone; Sylphara Voss once you are Noted; Lillith once the Unsworn know you; Elysomnion and Aurelia only at the top of their meters. None of them arrives to refuse.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_signal_benches: The signaller sells a compass for four emeralds and an echo shard at master. The splicer is a cleric by other means: glow berries in, ghast tears and a sculk catalyst out.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_void_benches: The voidwright turns raw iron and gold into ingots and sells diamond at 30. The hydroponicist buys wheat and kelp, and at master an enchanted golden apple for sixty emeralds.
elysiumalmanac.why.court_wanderer: He buys what you have too much of and sells what is tedious rather than hard: a nautilus shell, a name tag, a saddle, powder snow. None of it is powerful; all of it is a Saturday saved.
elysiumalmanac.why.crack_it: Ten oil in, five rocket fuel and five diesel out, for 100 FE, every five ticks. Both products need room or neither is made, so give the diesel somewhere to go.
elysiumalmanac.why.crank: Every machine in the first age is turned by something. A crank is the something you can afford on day one.
elysiumalmanac.why.creosote_engine: It turns 160 rpm free with 48 of torque, burns everything up to creosote, and wants brass under it. A bigger engine is not much more efficient: it is more powerful, and thirstier.
elysiumalmanac.why.crowned_heads: A head may be three times the hardest beast of its rung and no more. The graftprime and breachprime carry 194 health and two phases, and what answers the first never answers the second.
elysiumalmanac.why.crusher: What the millstone becomes, at industrial scale and on a wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.diesel_power: Five mB of diesel every ten ticks for 400 FE: 40 a tick, twice a coal generator, and a full 10,000 mB tank runs for 20,000 ticks. The refinery's by-product pays for the refinery.
elysiumalmanac.why.dig_steel: Steel ore lies in every biome of home, and on the Pale Moon. It smelts to an ingot that counts as steel wherever steel is asked for, which a rocket asks for in blocks.
elysiumalmanac.why.doctrine_and_doorway: A bulwark swings every 40 ticks where a harrier swings every 8. A gatekeeper mends between swings and an obstinate one is worst when nearly done. The adept makes all of them worse.
elysiumalmanac.why.downbloom_field: Nine tufts to a bale and the bale comes apart again, so a harvest keeps in a ninth of the room. The same eight stages and ripe-only rule as loomflax, and fortune folds in as it does on ore.
elysiumalmanac.why.drawer: A drawer holds one kind and thousands of it, costs nothing to run, and you can read how full it is across a room.
elysiumalmanac.why.dressed_stone: Pale, frost and cinder stone each cut to bricks, polished, chiseled, pillars, slabs and stairs on the stonecutter. Carrying stone up a gravity well is a mistake you make once.
elysiumalmanac.why.driven_rock: Tier 1: 3,600 an hour for 64 FE on the low grid, at whatever share the grid can spare. Half fed, it makes half as much rather than stopping.
elysiumalmanac.why.earth_and_plaster: Dirt, gravel and clay make four rammed earth; clay and bone meal four pale plaster, which throws daylight back into a room. Seven copper make four grating to walk on over the machines.
elysiumalmanac.why.eleven_new_metals: Tin, zinc, nickel, silver, lead, aluminium, osmium, platinum, lithium, crimson iron, azure silver: raw ore to ingot in 200 ticks, or 100 blasted.
elysiumalmanac.why.emberwood_charcoal: A log in a furnace for 200 ticks, and what comes out burns 2400 where coal burns 1600. A farmable fuel better than coal is the reward for carrying a sapling out of the Nether.
elysiumalmanac.why.emberwood_found: Emberwood grows where nothing else does, in the Nether and on Cinderveil. An axe strips the log and the wood like any other. The point of the tree is what it burns as.
elysiumalmanac.why.emberwood_joinery: Slab, stairs, fence, gate, door, trapdoor, button and pressure plate, in every tag the oak ones are in, so a villager opens the door and the fence meets the oak one next door.
elysiumalmanac.why.emberwood_planks: Planks burn 300 ticks like any plank; the virtue is in the log, not the board. But it is a dark wood the game does not have, and every shape below is cut from it.
elysiumalmanac.why.emberwood_planted: Carry a sapling home and it grows in a field like oak; bone meal brings it on in about ten goes. From then on the tree is farmable, which is the whole reason to have gone below for it.
elysiumalmanac.why.emerald_bastion: 92,000 megametres, or 1,889 from Frostfall. Full gravity, good air, no hazard at all and nothing hostile spawns at any light. Moss for grass, deepslate for stone, and emerald in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.emgrove: A mangrove with green wood, standing on its roots in groves across the Bastion. It strips with an axe and planks four to a log, and a propagule takes the tree home.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_aetherium: Eight veins a chunk from y -32 to 64. Light and planar, tier one, Dimensional: 24 armour to netherite's 20, and enchantability rather than knockback resistance.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_archive: Both meters, both bands, your floor and what moved them lately, in one place. It also hands out contracts, a cull or a survey or a delivery, paid in emeralds and standing.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_area_tools: A hammer breaks a 3x3 face, a spear digs one, a scythe harvests one, a broadaxe fells the whole tree. Tin to tungsten come from other mods, and /elysium materials says which are here.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_claim: Every square of 128 blocks tallies ten a machine and three a loud block, and at 120 a survey finds it. A beacon, used, files 64 blocks round it, clears the tally and floors Suspicion at 8 or more.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_crown: No recipe. It comes off a named enforcer four times in a hundred, and only while you are Hunted, so letting the meter fall ends the chase. Unique, fireproof, and Elysomnion's own.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_cutting: Dust climbs a rune's purity at the cutting table, priced like the forge's merge. Four dust and a pearl make a socket; blaze powder an affix level; a ghast tear takes a rune back out.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_elemental_arms: Five elements, each ahead of two others. The Singularity Lance is one enormous slow blow, the Neural Cascade Rifle half the weight at twice the rate. Every raider carries one of the five.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_enforcer: Past 25 Suspicion one may be sent every ten seconds, up to four at Hunted, in more of the plate at each band. Killing one is twelve Suspicion more, so it escalates rather than ends.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_hazards: A day is four watches; each has a storm or not, a fifth arriving and a fifth leaving. The built answers are a matching armour set, a shelter with a bed and a light, and a filed claim.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_imperial_gear: Thirteen shapes in each material. A rune of the piece's own element is worth more in it: a Voidward rune in a voidglass hammer is aligned, the same rune in an iron one is not.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_inspection: Mine sixty-four ores in five minutes while on file and the Empire plants one. Within 48 blocks ore costs double for twenty minutes. Breaking it works, and somebody is sent to ask why.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_neutronium: Three veins a chunk below y 16, absurdly dense, tier two and Kinetic. An enforcer drops an ingot one kill in three, which is the other way to get it and the louder one.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_noticed: Every ore is two Suspicion and a rich one four. Past 25 you are Noted, 50 Marked, 75 Hunted, and the meter bleeds a point every two minutes, but never below 25 once you are on file.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_plate: Two pieces give a tenth of knockback resistance, four add two toughness and shrug off part of every blast. The Voidweave Aegis is seven voidglass round a neutronium block, and Legendary.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_raider: Squads roam every two to four minutes whatever you have done. A named raider is four Favor, an ordinary hostile one a third of the time; Favor raises the tier of what everything drops.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_ramp: Copper carries Plasma, iron Kinetic, gold Neural, diamond Dimensional, netherite Void. The ramp sockets, reforges and asks a level like the Empire's own, so the elements are learnt early.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_rations: Bread and two of something: snowballs for thermal, charcoal for cryogenic, honeycomb, kelp or clay for the other three. Three minutes immune to that one hazard, and about a potato's worth of food.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_reforge: A catalyst rerolls a piece's three bonuses, keeping runes and ascension, and each piece has only so many charges. With Silent Gear installed, a template carries gear across the seam.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_regalia: Raiders at Favoured wear the helm and at Exalted the carapace, and three in a hundred let go. Two pieces give a heart; four give six per cent to dodge and a burst of speed.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_runes: Four voidglass round one thing: an ender pearl for Voidward, a blaze rod for Plasmaforge. Five follow the elements; four do what no attribute can, from a dodge to a shield that rebuilds.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_scanner: Point it at a creature, a plant, an ore or a structure to put it on record. The Empire pays most and notices you, the Unsworn pay less and like you for it, nobody pays nothing.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_sockets: Runes go into gear at the socket table. At the forge two runes of a tier become one of the next, and two identical pieces become one a tier higher, which the Empire notices.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_spawners: A brutal spawner sends four waves of two, promoted; a swarm six waves of six. A caged invader does nothing until broken, then lets an elite out. One of each in about 26 chunks, underground.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_voidglass: Five veins a chunk between y -48 and 32, and it drops the ingot itself, cut rather than cast. The Empire's first material: diamond's protection, a little less durable, and Void.
elysiumalmanac.why.empire_wounds: A heavy blow leaves a heart short, a fall a tenth slower, fire slower hands, a blast slower swings. Capped, never copied on death, and they mend four times as fast in a med bay.
elysiumalmanac.why.enricher: The last rung of the ore ladder. Nothing above this does better.
elysiumalmanac.why.equipment_and_office: An interdictor drone carries a field of 4 a level that soaks the first blows. A lictor is the most armoured thing here; an aegis stands in a doorway and is the doorway.
elysiumalmanac.why.every_shape_of_it: A starsteel gear is four ingots of an alloy of an alloy of an alloy, and a tier four casing asks 4,096 FE of the grid. Nothing in the chain sits above either of them.
elysiumalmanac.why.fallen_things: Meteors in six shapes, a fallen satellite and an operation base, all at home. Somebody was going up before you were, and left the evidence lying about where you can dig it out.
elysiumalmanac.why.far_waters: Lava is a body of liquid and has things living in it here. The rarest fish in any water shows inside 400 casts, and the checker holds every table to that, this one included.
elysiumalmanac.why.farms: A villager farm turns one seed into three crop every 600 ticks, exactly what a farmer does by hand; the iron farm makes an ingot every five minutes. Neither multiplies emeralds, on purpose.
elysiumalmanac.why.fast_and_frail: A scavenger is barely a fight alone, which is the point of it. A harrier stopped trying to out-hit anyone: the swiftblade runs at 1.4 speed on 0.65 of the health.
elysiumalmanac.why.faster_never_a_wall: Amounts climb and shares curve. Swarming adds one a step for ever; haste halves the wait at four steps and never goes under 10 ticks, so a spawner tuned for ever never becomes a wall.
elysiumalmanac.why.fed_and_turning: Fed 4,096 FE it drives a line to 1,024 rpm with 384 of torque, and says what it is fed and how fast it turns. A works on a shaft wants 256 rpm before it moves at all.
elysiumalmanac.why.fill_a_room: It fills a closed room: 1 mB and 5 FE for each new block, then 1 mB per 400 blocks a scan to keep it. A torch does not seal a room, a shut door does. A suit refills inside at 100 a second.
elysiumalmanac.why.first_blade: Six shapes of weapon here, and this is the quick one. It does less per hit than almost anything else and gets more hits in than all of it.
elysiumalmanac.why.first_essence: A seed takes 12,000 ticks a crop and pays one essence. Four of a tier make a seed of the next, eight make the material itself; tin, zinc and lead come as chunks the foundry smelts.
elysiumalmanac.why.first_flight: Fuel it, sit in it, press H: ten seconds, a climb, and a list of only what the tank reaches. High Orbit is 0.4 megametres up and costs one millibucket. Choose nothing and it lands.
elysiumalmanac.why.first_rod: Reed, oak, iron, steel, starsteel: five rungs of luck counting the bare hook as the first. Each tilts the table 0.34 towards the rare end and never removes a common fish.
elysiumalmanac.why.food_book: Thirty different foods for ten extra hearts, the same thing twice counting once. The curve is a square root: the first ten are worth 5.8 hearts, the last ten 1.6. Use it to see where you are.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_alloy: Hold a part of mixed materials and hit the forge. It earns up to a tenth more for every material past the first, scaled by how much they have in common. A part of one material is told there is nothing to gain.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_armour: Five materials for a helmet's plates, eight for a chestplate's. Armour carries its traits the same way a blade does: bounce boots take no fall damage, moonwalker lightens the fall, snow walker stays on top.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_blueprint: Three paper and a clay ball make three sheets; one sheet at the bench is a blueprint for one part. Lay it in a grid with the materials and the part comes out and so does the blueprint.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_first_tool: A head of three materials, a rod, and the grid assembles them. Every number on it is worked out from what went in. It never breaks: it stops one point short, broken and waiting to be repaired.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_fittings: Binding, grip, tip, coating, lining: one material each, bolted on. The mod kit takes the last one off whole. Upgrades: magnetic, a spoon for a pickaxe, a wider plate, and a red card that lets it break.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_grader: Part in the main hand, a gem in the other, spent either way. Each grade E to A is worth six per cent. The first try fails one time in nine and leaves it Crude, ten per cent worse; later ones just fail.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_jewellery: Shank, band or chain of metal, and a setting on top. A ring, bracelet or necklace is worn in its own slot and carries its materials' traits the way a blade does; moonwalker works from a ring.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_masterwork: Graded to A, charged under the stars, forged for synergy and rerolled until the affixes suit: a part can come out nearly half again what its metal alone would make. Build a full set that way.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_press: Hold ingots, hit the press, get sheet metal. No screen, one input, one output, and ten ticks between strokes so it cannot empty a chest in a second. Sheet is a material the plates and wings take.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_ranged: Bow, crossbow, slingshot, trident, rod and the arrow itself, each built like a blade is. Limbs take three materials and cord three more, so the string is a choice as much as the wood is.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_reforge: The essence you put in is the rarity you get: five is Legendary. Three results at once, and the same three until the inputs change, so closing and reopening the table buys nothing.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_salvage: An untouched piece gives each part back three times in four, a nearly broken one once in four. Affixes were never parts: they come back as essence, one per level, which is what a reroll is paid in.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_shield_wings: A shield plate is two materials. Wings are six, and only cloth or sheet will do. A built elytra wears as it flies, like the game's own, and like every built piece stops one point short of breaking.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_smithing_table: The table draws all forty-eight parts, not only the rough ones. A plan book eats a blueprint and keeps it for good, and stands in for any plan it has learned, which empties a pocket of paper.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_starlight: Lay a part on it and walk away. It counts only night it can see: 6,000 ticks of open sky and the part is starcharged, worth fifteen per cent more on top of its grade, once. Under a roof it waits for ever.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_stone_anvil: Seven cobblestone, no iron anywhere in it. It draws plans only for what rock, wood, bone and fibre can make, which is a stone axe and not much else. The first thing you build and the last you use.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_weapons: Seven shapes, from a knife to a mace, and over a hundred materials to make them of. The traits come with the material: malleable iron sometimes shrugs off wear, adamant hits the big things harder.
elysiumalmanac.why.forge_wide: A hammer breaks a square, an excavator a square of soil, a saw a tree, a paxel is three tools; the prospector's hammer reports what is in the rock. Each one wears for the blocks it takes.
elysiumalmanac.why.found_not_made: Twenty-eight trinkets change a rule rather than an amount, and none can be made. One chest in twenty in an ancient city, bastion, end city, stronghold library or woodland mansion.
elysiumalmanac.why.four_gems: Bort, certus quartz, fluorite and rime shard come out of the furnace whole. One shape each and no further up the chain: they are here so that the ore that drops them drops something.
elysiumalmanac.why.four_notches: A dial, not a slider. One enriched uranium lasts 6,000 ticks at full and four times that at a quarter. The core reads its heat now and the heat this notch will settle at.
elysiumalmanac.why.four_turbines_in_one: 480 FE a tick on the medium wire, and it gets through the same fuel four times as fast. Not a better turbine: four of them in one block, on a wire you had to earn.
elysiumalmanac.why.freight: A chest of 27 stacks and 8,000 mB of fuel, three rockets in the air at most. Each stack adds 15% of the empty cost, so a full load is six times cheaper a stack. The moon is 35 seconds.
elysiumalmanac.why.frost_raptor: Twenty health, three damage, two blocks tall and not in a hurry. It is not the raptor that kills people on Frostfall; it is the cold while they fight it.
elysiumalmanac.why.frost_temples: A great temple and lesser ones, a maze cut into the ground, towers and ruins. Whoever built them built for the cold, which is the first thing to copy.
elysiumalmanac.why.frostfall: 55,700 megametres, which is 2,899 of a basic tank's 3,000 from home: the trip that teaches refuelling. 0.38 gravity, thin air, and cold and radiation both at full strength.
elysiumalmanac.why.frostite: Two metals in the red regolith, with iron, diamond, rime and plutonium beside them. Cryonite is what a waygate frame is made of. Whiteouts come through, and a wall is the answer.
elysiumalmanac.why.fuel: One piece runs a reactor at full throttle for five minutes. You will want a supply before you light one.
elysiumalmanac.why.fuel_refinery: A coal block in, creosote out 300 ticks later, and the line must hold 48 rpm. A coal block burns 16,000 ticks; creosote burns 24,000. That difference is what the refinery is for.
elysiumalmanac.why.full_at_a_glance: The front shows how full it is in five steps, and a comparator reads the same. A wall of them tells you what is running low from across the room, which is the point of a wall.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_first_cluster: Every random tick is one chance in thirty for each open face: a small bud, a medium, a large, a cluster. Break the cluster for four shards. Break its support and it drops the four anyway.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_glass: Four shards round a block of glass make two, in the colour of whatever the shards were: thirty windows, and somewhere to spend the shards a geode grows faster than you use them.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_relic_diamond: Diamond shards buy the third rarity, and these are pressed: blinkstep boots every ten seconds, a shockwave every fifteen. The phoenix down is the exception and fires by itself below three tenths of your health.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_relic_emerald: Emerald shards. The storm-caller's rod every forty seconds, the sanctuary bell once a minute on a sneak, the warden's regalia three abilities at once. Rarity is how much a relic does per press, not per minute.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_relic_gold: Gold shards buy the second rarity, relics that go off on their own: a riposte when you are hurt, a cleave when you hit, a pulse of warding every twenty seconds. Each has a cooldown the tooltip states.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_relic_iron: Four iron shards and four gold ingots. The commonest relics work while carried and do one thing for good: the wanderer's charm makes you quicker, the diving bell lets you breathe, the lamp lets you see.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_seed_given: Two to four blocks of the material's own shards and a glow ink sac make a budding block. Its own shards and nothing else, so a geode multiplies what you have and is never a back door to what you have not.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_seed_mined: What the foundry mines costs dearer: twenty to thirty-two shards and an echo shard from the deep dark. It pays for itself in five to eight clusters and grows for ever after, and breaking it gives it back.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_shards: Thirty materials: twenty the foundry mines and ten the game digs up, each with a shard, a block of four shards and a way back. The block is what a seeding is paid in, so this is the unit to save in.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_spyglass: One shard on two copper ingots, where the game's own spyglass takes amethyst. Thirty of them, one to a material, which makes a spyglass the way to show what your geodes grow.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_tenth: Spend motes on anything you have dissolved before. A round trip loses a tenth and no recipe is ever worth more than it costs, so over a million random acts nobody's estate has gone up. Motes survive death.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_too_soon: A bud broken at any of its three sizes gives nothing at all, with silk touch or without. The lesson costs one bud, and the budding block puts out another on the next lucky tick.
elysiumalmanac.why.geode_transmuter: Obsidian, diamonds and a nether star. Put something in and most of its worth comes back as motes, a cobblestone being one and an iron ingot 256. Anything the table cannot price is refused rather than guessed at.
elysiumalmanac.why.governor: Five classes: critical, defence, logistics, industry, comfort. A governor says when this, hold that class and everything below it. A fresh one holds comfort, always, so the lamps go first.
elysiumalmanac.why.gravel_pile: Cobblestone to gravel in 120 ticks at a slow pace, a bone to four meal, a blaze rod to four powder once the line is steady. A recipe names a pace, never a raw rpm.
elysiumalmanac.why.ground_fine: The crusher takes any ingot of the chain to dust in 100 ticks, and dust smelts back in 200 or blasts in 100. Coal dust is what steel and cast iron are alloyed with.
elysiumalmanac.why.half_a_skeleton: Seven fossils, each a skull and a body. One half gives 0.4 of the effect, the pair all of it, and never from further than eight blocks: a fossil is something you arrange, not a switch.
elysiumalmanac.why.harvest: Onion is the quick one at 1,800 ticks, ginger the slow one at 3,600, rice the only crop that wants a paddy, and none of them beats wheat on every axis. Nine of anything to a crate.
elysiumalmanac.why.harvesters: Nine by nine for 60 FE a plant, one seed back in the ground each time. A tree is logs on soil, six leaves and under 512 blocks, 400 FE apiece, and a house fails all three.
elysiumalmanac.why.hauler: A truck, two more motors and more plate: 18 blocks a second and 54 slots. Off the road it keeps half that on open ground and under a third on rough, which is why the road came first.
elysiumalmanac.why.heat_goes_as_the_cube: A five-cube holds 27 rods and takes 25 channels, and is safe to 89 per cent. A seven holds 125 and is safe below 38. Rods go as the cube and cooling as the square.
elysiumalmanac.why.heavier_motors: Uranium, plutonium and heavy metal motors burn their own metal: a nugget a canister, an ingot nine. Plutonium goes 29.3 megametres a millibucket. Heavy metal is uranium, neptunium, plutonium.
elysiumalmanac.why.heavy_and_unseen: A reaver wants you cornered, and a slagfist takes three quarters from a blade and a quarter more from fire. A whisper is dangerous until it is noticed; a gutterghost blinds you as it goes.
elysiumalmanac.why.hive: Two flowers a bee. Too few and it slows down rather than stopping, so go and plant something.
elysiumalmanac.why.hold_it_up: Right-click holding what you want: a stack, or one if you crouch. It answers in steps and machine-runs before it moves a thing, or names exactly what is missing.
elysiumalmanac.why.hooks: Sneak and use the rod with a part in the other hand. Iron is worth a rung, gilded two, a barbed hook holds the bite until you reel in, a double brings up two. The box takes tackle and nothing else.
elysiumalmanac.why.hydrogen_motor: Diamonds, a lunite block and rime. It burns hydrogen canisters at 21.36 megametres a millibucket against fuel's 19.22. Empty the tank before you fit it: two fuels never share one.
elysiumalmanac.why.in_batches: A job goes out in batches small enough for one set of slots. The rest stays in the drawers where you can still use it, and a mined assembler loses a batch at most, never the order.
elysiumalmanac.why.industrial_apiary: Twenty-four bees, six slots, and fully fitted it lands on a quarter of a mine and not a comb over, which is not a number anybody chose. Eighteen thousand combinations are swept to prove it.
elysiumalmanac.why.industrial_rock: Tier 2: 14,400 blocks an hour for 128 FE. This is where stone stops being something you go and get and becomes something you pipe.
elysiumalmanac.why.insanium: Four ascendant essences on four pedestals make one insanium, which is exactly what a rung costs everywhere else on the ladder. The altar is not a discount.
elysiumalmanac.why.invar: Two iron and a nickel. What a second-tier machine casing is.
elysiumalmanac.why.jet_suit: A chestplate with fins, two engines and a blaze rod, and its own 2,000 mB tank of fuel canisters. J cycles flight, hover and off. Hovering sinks slowly, burns half as much, and takes no fall.
elysiumalmanac.why.keen_essence: Deep, cold or somewhere else entirely: platinum, uranium, uraninite, bort, rime shard, azure silver, diamond and emerald. Eight times the wait of the first rung.
elysiumalmanac.why.keep_bees: Twelve bees, two flowers each within five blocks, one comb per bee every 3,000 ticks; too few flowers and it slows in proportion. A scoop takes a finished comb off a bee in the air.
elysiumalmanac.why.keep_it_awake: It keeps its own chunk loaded while a line turns it, for 6 torque at 48 rpm. When the line stops it holds on 200 ticks more, so a windmill losing the wind does not drop the farm.
elysiumalmanac.why.killing_them_for_you: A grinder saw doubles the drops and leaves every orb; spikes leave half. A killer that took the orbs would make the spallet the only thing worth farming. The press keeps the orbs to carry.
elysiumalmanac.why.kindreds: Twenty-seven creatures in thirteen kindreds, and no two of a kindred share a trait or a home: the ferricbarb poisons in the open, the rimebarb freezes in the snow. Same rung, another fight.
elysiumalmanac.why.knife: Flint, iron, gold, diamond, netherite: a board asks only whether it is a knife, and each cut wears it by one. The fillet knife is for the hook, and lasts 240 fish.
elysiumalmanac.why.landing_sites: The first landing, an old launch pad, a space base, a sphere, two villages (one ruined), a wrecked ship and two dungeons. Most of them have chests, and nobody is coming back for them.
elysiumalmanac.why.large_tank: Seven lunite and a bucket, used on an idle rocket: 6,000 mB instead of 3,000. Home to the Bastion is 4,787 on plain fuel, and this is the only tank that holds it in one go.
elysiumalmanac.why.launch_pad: Three iron and three smooth stone make four. A rocket will not launch from anything else. Crouch and use an idle rocket nobody is sitting in to pick it back up.
elysiumalmanac.why.lay_the_bus: A controller indexes 64 devices along its bus at 1.5 FE each, and past that it refuses rather than slows. A dyed run joins only its own colour or plain bus, so two networks can share a wall.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_callings: Medicae heal everyone within eight blocks, Factors take a second drop a quarter of the time, Reclaimers a second ingot one vein in four, Artificers reforge half again higher. The rest fight.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_codex: Handed over on the first join with eight bread and sixteen torches, and never crafted: lose it and /elysium sheet opens the same pages. It is the only book in the pack about you.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_declare: The screen on first join asks for one origin and one calling, and it is recorded once. The answer puts two starts on the Ledger Web in your name, free, for good.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_erasure: Two paper, a book and two gem dust strike one entry. Right-click a node you hold to give it back: it must be a leaf, and a start is never given back. Walked back, but not for free.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_every_action: Mining, digging, building, crafting, smelting, harvesting, fishing, taming, breeding, trading, enchanting, eating and a new biome all pay, each capped per minute so none of them is a farm.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_first_level: A level costs 100 plus ten for every level you already have, so the second takes 110. A kill pays 4, a named combatant 14, an ore 6. There is no ceiling at all.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_gem_case: Eight voidglass round a chest, and it behaves like a bundle that refuses everything but runes, sigils and dust. It is not a backpack, and it will not let you pretend it is.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_gem_dust: A rune ground down in the crafting grid, no bench needed. It returns what the rune cost in base runes less a quarter, so dust moves value between runes and never makes any.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_keystone: Twelve keystones off the rim of ring two, in six opposed pairs: Sanctioned or Clandestine, Bonded or Freehold. Each gains twelve of one stat, loses six of another, and bars its opposite.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_level_five: Five hundred experience from the start, forty stat points assigned by hand and twelve web points to spend. The bars on the sheet are drawn against your own largest stat, not a fixed fifty.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_level_ten: Ten levels to a world tier: from here the world answers in Ascent, and everything drops at the tier your level and your holdings say. /elysium tier shows how far along the share you are.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_notable: Ring one has a cluster per stat, ring two one per system: the Seam, the Line, the Weather, the Kitchen. The notable at a cluster's heart is five of two stats, and names the cluster.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_origins: Imperial answers harm done to it; Druun hit harder as they bleed; Veylari ignore ten blocks of any fall; Korrath heal triple when left alone; Lumari shield double; Unsworn are forgotten fast.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_research: Six fields, Geology to Rift Science, each climbing from Unstudied to Preeminent by doing the thing rather than by levelling. A rank unlocks a reading: a hazard's number, a vein's depth.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_stats: Twelve stats and nothing caps one: every effect runs value over value plus a halfway mark, so it approaches its ceiling and never arrives. /elysium respec hands every point back at once.
elysiumalmanac.why.ledger_web_tab: Three web points a level from level two, on top of the ten stat points. Click a lit node: lit means it touches something you hold. A small node is two of one stat.
elysiumalmanac.why.let_it_press: Quintuple is 59,049 blocks, octuple 43 million. Nobody crafts that by hand: queue it on the terminal and let the assemblers press it while the warehouse fills.
elysiumalmanac.why.light_by_the_row: A candle holder is 6 in any colour, soul 4, cupric 7, ender 9, a candelabra 12; lanterns 9 and 12, lamps 13 and 14. Nothing reaches 15, and at 7 most of the dark still spawns.
elysiumalmanac.why.longbow_and_recurve: A longbow does 12 at 0.8 draws a second and halves your pace while drawn; a recurve 6 at 1.6 and carries furthest of all. Barbed arrows bleed, ember burn, rime slow, thunder chains.
elysiumalmanac.why.longsword_shape: The shape that is best at nothing: 6.5 a hit at 1.9 swings a second and a quarter-block more reach. Against a diamond sword's 7 at 1.6, it is what to carry when you do not know what is coming.
elysiumalmanac.why.look_up: There are five worlds besides this one, and waygates that open at ruined-portal frequency. Go and find one.
elysiumalmanac.why.loomflax_field: Farmland only; on grass it pops. Eight stages, fibre only at the last and seeds back at any, so breaking it early is a replant and not a loss. Bone meal hurries it like wheat.
elysiumalmanac.why.low_meets_medium: The one block allowed two voltages on it. A copper grid on one side and a gold one on the other become one supply; put the same two wires together anywhere else and nothing flows.
elysiumalmanac.why.luna: No air, no weather, and a crop that grows in vacuum and nothing else.
elysiumalmanac.why.lunite: The moon's metal, with iron, steel and rime shard in the same rock. Lunite is what the tank upgrade, every motor, the waygate anchor and half of a station are made of.
elysiumalmanac.why.make_rock: Tier 0: 900 blocks an hour for nothing at all, held in one slot until something takes them. The stone generator is the same rate in stone, the one vein that is free.
elysiumalmanac.why.metal_veins: Raw copper worth 30 per cent of a mine's hour, raw iron 22, and the build refuses any vein that beats its share. Tier 1 generators, 64 FE each.
elysiumalmanac.why.mill_race: Flowing water only, at least two blocks of it round the rim: a wheel in a pond is a wheel nothing pushes. Sixteen rpm free and 48 of stall torque. Slow, strong, and free forever.
elysiumalmanac.why.millstone: Cobblestone to gravel, bone to meal, ore to more ore later. The first machine that pays for itself.
elysiumalmanac.why.moon_rock: Regolith over pale stone over pale deepslate, at 0.165 of the gravity you are used to. Pale vines hang in the hollows and light them when they fruit, the way cave vines do at home.
elysiumalmanac.why.moonfolk: Moonfolk trade and build no golems; the hollow ones spit rime from fifteen blocks for two damage and a chill. A void crawler has forty health, bites for nine, and arrows glance off it.
elysiumalmanac.why.more_storage: A shelf costs six eighths of a block and breaking one gives nothing back; a cabinet or a crate costs a whole block and gives one. No recipe here makes more than it takes, and that is proved.
elysiumalmanac.why.motor: Electricity back into rotation. Your first machine hall does not stop being useful — it stops being hand-cranked.
elysiumalmanac.why.moving_them: A mob fan pushes and a conveyor carries, and neither changes what anything is worth. Quiet casing and dread soil decide where things spawn, and nothing about what they pay.
elysiumalmanac.why.named_in_diamond: Nine at diamond, each an ordinary weapon of its shape that also does one thing: duelist's grace ripostes, emberline brands, frostpike chills. Never a better weapon, only a different one.
elysiumalmanac.why.named_in_netherite: Eight at the top, allowed twice what a diamond legend may carry: worldsplitter's shockwave, mountainfall's bulwark, gravebolt's gravewake. Each tier's band is half the one above it.
elysiumalmanac.why.nest: Four wild bees: meadow in plains, forest, stone in mountains, water by rivers. A nest is one in 24 chunks, holds three, grows one back every 6,000 ticks; an empty jar takes one.
elysiumalmanac.why.never_again_spiders: A stack of string and a stack of charcoal, grown rather than found. Every bow, bed and torch from here comes off a field, and the furnace runs on a tree you can replant.
elysiumalmanac.why.nine_into_one: Nine of anything the game hands out by the thousand make one compressed block, and it comes apart again on a grid. Sixty materials, each wearing the face of the thing it is made of.
elysiumalmanac.why.ninths: An ingot breaks into nine and nine make it back. A ninth is the unit everything in the chain is priced in, so a gear worth four ingots is 36 of them and every sum is whole.
elysiumalmanac.why.no_wire_at_all: Put an engine's brass shaft into a crusher and it runs with no wire in sight: 96 rpm or nothing, and 45 per cent of what a wire would give. A fallback, not a plan.
elysiumalmanac.why.nodding_donkey: 10 mB a tick for 10 FE from the chunk it stands in. Half of all chunks are dry; the rest hold 1,000 to 40,000 mB, fixed by the seed, and it says how much is left when you ask.
elysiumalmanac.why.nonuple: Nine tiers down: 387,420,489 of a thing in one block, and a good deal harder to explain than to mine. The bottom of the ladder. There is no tenth.
elysiumalmanac.why.noon_and_midnight: Three FE a tick under open sky and nothing at night or in shade, checked once a second. A panel is a trickle into a cell, and that is all it was ever meant to be.
elysiumalmanac.why.old_places: A keep is the largest thing standing, up to twenty rooms with a watch on top and cellars under. A mine runs sixteen rooms down, a ruin eleven, a shrine six and ends in one.
elysiumalmanac.why.on_a_water_wheel: Nothing below 48 rpm, then 1.5 FE a tick for every rpm, and it takes 60 torque off the line to do it. Six times a dynamo for six times the draw, so one engine is rarely enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.on_the_hands: An executioner's grip lands critical blows at 1.5 times and more as it ascends; a miner's rig spares a fifth of a tool's wear. A ratchet gauntlet hits far harder on a crit and softer otherwise.
elysiumalmanac.why.on_the_head: A neural filament raises experience a fifth, an artificer's loupe reforges a fifth better. Longsight teaches faster and hits softer; the prospector's lens pays ore twice and teaches less.
elysiumalmanac.why.on_the_road: A cart does 6 blocks a second on paving, 9 slots, one seat, and burns anything a furnace does: a coal is sixteen of its 200. On grass it does 3, slower than the 4.3 you walk.
elysiumalmanac.why.open_the_grave: Up to 512 stacks, moved at most five blocks to somewhere it can stand and never into the void. Yours alone for thirty minutes, then anybody's. It keeps three quarters of your experience.
elysiumalmanac.why.oven: Slowest, 500 to 800 ticks, four servings, and bacon and ham cure here. Stuffed pumpkin is 13 nutrition, the best meal in the pack. A cabinet is a chest with a door: 27 stacks, any wood.
elysiumalmanac.why.pack_it_down: Every metal out here comes raw, as an ingot, as nine nuggets and as a block, and its raw ore packs nine to a block as well. A rocket's hold is small; blocks are how it goes home.
elysiumalmanac.why.parcels: A paper box holds nine stacks and costs no postage because it is never posted. A package is the same nine stacks sent, for four paper, which is still cheaper per stack than a letter.
elysiumalmanac.why.payback: The other end has 30, 180 or 4320 minutes to pay, and the shortest is longer than the slowest delivery. Fifteen parcels in a thousand go astray and come back as lost mail worth a quarter.
elysiumalmanac.why.pigeonhole: A pigeon rests 6000 ticks after a delivery, which is the only reason to keep two. Carry one below and in 300 ticks it is a charred pigeon; carry it home and it turns back.
elysiumalmanac.why.plate: You will need a great deal of it. A factory is a thing you build with a factory.
elysiumalmanac.why.pockets: Small adds nine slots, large eighteen, deep twenty-seven, and a bag holds exactly what is fitted. A pocket will not come out while what it holds would have nowhere to go.
elysiumalmanac.why.pot: One block, stackable in a room, feedable by a hopper. It wants light 9 or nothing grows.
elysiumalmanac.why.press_and_loom: Eight leaves press to a fibre for 800 FE; six dried kelp for 720. The loom weaves two fibres into three string for 320, four into two wool for 480, and never resets a run on a full tray.
elysiumalmanac.why.pull_it_in: Placed against a chest, it pulls a stack a second into the network. Right-click it holding something and it takes only that; right-click it empty-handed and it forgets.
elysiumalmanac.why.push_it_out: The other way: a stack a second of the thing it was shown, into whatever it faces. Shown nothing, it does nothing, because everything you own into one furnace is never what you meant.
elysiumalmanac.why.radiant_essence: The ones worth a trip: gold, osmium, amethyst, fluorite, certus quartz, obsidian and crimson iron, at four times the wait of a copper seed and still under two thirds of a mine.
elysiumalmanac.why.reactor: Prod it: it tells you the temperature now and the one this setting will reach. Do the arithmetic before you turn it up.
elysiumalmanac.why.reclaimer: A millibucket a tick for 8 FE, four times that in rain, into a tank of eight buckets. With a bucket in it, it counts as a bioreactor's water, and it fills a cauldron beside it.
elysiumalmanac.why.repeater_and_crossbow: A repeater looses three at once for 3.5 each. A crossbow does 10, is the only one that is perfectly accurate, and takes bolts no bow will: iron, piercing and shattering.
elysiumalmanac.why.rich_loam: The third tier of soil: 1.7 times the speed of dirt, and it grows the common, the crops, the hardy and the desert things. Only the fungal and the end are beyond it.
elysiumalmanac.why.rich_veins: Gold at 15 per cent of a mine, diamond 6, emerald 5, netherite scrap 2. The fraction shrinks as the material improves, because the point of a deep mine is that the good things are deep.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_boss: A dais ringed with light, nowhere to hide, and at the end of the longest walk a Choir or a Praetor at the dungeon's own level. The boss is placed before the loot so the longest walk never ends in a chest.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_cartography: With the Rift Cartography unlock a dungeon tells you on arrival how many loot rooms it has and how deep it goes: the difference between leaving satisfied and leaving wondering what was left.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_denizens: A room by the door holds one or two; a room by the boss a handful, never more than nine. Past the second room one in four is an elite: a lictor or a bulwark where a drone would have been.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_frame: Four obsidian, four deepslate bricks and an ender pearl make four frames. Ten makes the smallest ring, the same shape as a Nether portal: two wide and three high inside.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_key: An eye of ender, a gold ingot and two iron. Sixty-four openings: it is worn, not spent, so a run costs durability rather than a trip to the bench.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_leave: Walk out through the return rift, die or log off: once the last of you has left, that dungeon is over and the next step through builds a new one. A friend who joins one already standing does not refill it.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_loot: Three to a dungeon, at the dead ends, deepest first. What is in them is whatever the pack has offered for your tier, which is where affixed gear comes from and so where essence for a reroll comes from.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_open: Any rectangle from two by three up to twenty-one square inside. A frame one short says so on the action bar rather than doing nothing. Break any frame block and the rift closes within the tick.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_rooms: Sealed rooms twenty-one across and nine high, joined only by doorways. The entrance first, the boss at the furthest cell by doors walked, three loot rooms at the deepest dead ends, filler everywhere else.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_second_door: Rift Science is credited once per portal, so commuting through your own rift teaches nothing new. A second frame somewhere else does. Sixty ticks after travel a rift ignores you, so it cannot bounce you back.
elysiumalmanac.why.rift_through: Twenty rooms built fresh, at their own cell of a grid 1,024 blocks from the last, from a seed never used before. Stepping into a rift is also how Rift Science is learned.
elysiumalmanac.why.road: A road is worth laying because of how much of a journey it saves, which means it is worth most to whatever is slowest. Build it before the vehicle, not after.
elysiumalmanac.why.rock: Everybody builds a cobblestone generator anyway. This one is a block, and it has tiers.
elysiumalmanac.why.rocket_built: The cone on top, a steel block in the middle, four fins and the engine. It holds 3,000 mB, which on plain fuel is 57,660 megametres of reach and says exactly where that gets you.
elysiumalmanac.why.rocket_parts: All of it steel: ingots for the cone and the fins, two steel blocks and a redstone for the engine. There is no rocket station; the parts go together on a crafting table.
elysiumalmanac.why.rolled_thin: The rolling mill takes one ingot to one plate in 120 ticks, for every metal the chain has. Plate is worth exactly its ingot, and every casing is skinned in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.rolling_mill: Plate is what every machine above this is skinned in. Nothing in the first age could make a sheet.
elysiumalmanac.why.rotten_wood_cracked_b: The dig's own building sets: rotten wood in every shape a wood comes in, cracked mud brick with a slab and a stair. Infested mud brick breaks at a touch and has something living in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.run_a_line: Cable carries 250 FE a tick and pipe 250 mB, to anybody's machines; a dye keeps two runs apart. The tank holds 16,000 mB of one fluid, keeps it when broken, and drains downward.
elysiumalmanac.why.sails: Sails in the plane the bearing turns in, touching it or each other. Each adds 6 torque and no speed, so sixteen carry 96 at 24 rpm. Past sixteen the bearing would tear itself off.
elysiumalmanac.why.saw: Six planks to a log instead of four, and the cheapest planks in the game from then on.
elysiumalmanac.why.screw_press: Slow by nature, so 16 rpm is enough and it draws 8. Sugar cane or bamboo to paper, a cactus to two green dye. The cheapest paper in the pack once a wheel is turning.
elysiumalmanac.why.sealed: A stamp is two wooden slabs and an iron ingot, pressed in wax, gold or lapis. Sealed, only the addressee opens it, and the seal is the service: a letter goes to two paper, a package to six.
elysiumalmanac.why.sealed_and_sieved: A sieve lets in only what the bag already holds. A void seal destroys what would not fit, and only of things already inside: for the cobblestone you are sick of, never a stray diamond.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_alloys: Always two things in a grid: cobalt and slag make slagsteel, cobalt and culture biolith, nightgold and a null shard nullsteel. Relicsteel is four relic shards and nothing else.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_cinder: Cinderveil's desert and barrens hold thirty-six, iron among them. A player who has reached a burning world should not have to go back to the Overworld for lead, and now does not.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_cobalt: The two Cordon metals come out raw and go through a furnace like iron. Cobalt is precious and the spine of every alloy below; pearlium is industrial and turns up in veins of seven.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_deeper: Seventeen ores in deepslate, among them the Cordon's own cobalt, jade and ruby. An ore only generates if something in the pack supplies its material, so nothing here is a block with no use.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_end: Thirty-eight ores in end stone, the most of any rock. The End used to be somewhere you went once, for a fight; now it is somewhere with a vein of platinum-bearing ground in every direction.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_experience: Experience marks the ores you do not smelt. Common and industrial pay nothing to two points, precious three to seven, exotic five to eleven, so a pickaxe that glows is telling you what kind of vein you are in.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_first_vein: Twelve materials go into plain stone, and every one is there because no other mod in the pack put it there. Common veins run nine blocks, exotic ones three, and a vein open to air loses half.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_found: Chitin off spiders, phasium off endermen, lattice only from an end city's treasure. Mireweave is the odd one: two bones and two string make two, the cheapest Cordon armour there is.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_frost: Frostfall's rock carries thirty-six. At tier six the bonus lands half the time, at eighteen three times in four, and never every time; the tier changes what mining pays, never whether it pays.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_gems: A gem ore drops the gem, finished. Silk touch keeps the ore itself; fortune multiplies the drop by two, three and so on with equal chance, and the worst roll is exactly what you had without it.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_nether: Thirty-seven ores in netherrack. The Nether used to have quartz and debris and nothing a tech mod eats; now it has lead, tin and uranium, and nobody walks home for them.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_nightgold: A gold ingot and a cobalt ingot make two nightgold in a crafting grid, no furnace. It is worn rather than swung, and it is half of both of the alloys at the top of the Cordon.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_pale: Thirty-six ores in the Pale Moon's stone. The deeper the world, the better the same vein pays: one more raw ore per three world tiers, landing tier in tier plus six of the time.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_roots: Six roots nothing digs: slag off a blaze, culture off a witch, shell off a guardian, crystal from an ancient city. One kill in thirty-three leaves one, one chest in sixteen.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_storage: Nine to a block and nine to an ingot, both ways, for every metal and gem the Cordon ships. Raw ore packs into a block too, which is the difference between one chest and two.
elysiumalmanac.why.seam_top: Nullsteel carries seventy-five Null defence and lattice a hundred, the two best materials the Cordoned Planet has. Four pyratite make one plate, for gear that is riveted rather than cast.
