elysiumalmanac.why.seam_unify: A big pack has five steels. One per family is chosen by a stated order of mods, every variant joins the tag, and each converts one for one. Type /elysium ores to see what was chosen and why.
elysiumalmanac.why.seed: Slowly, on purpose: a farm is meant to lose to a mine until it is a deliberate industrial project.
elysiumalmanac.why.separator: Ore in, twice the metal out. The reason the second age exists.
elysiumalmanac.why.servo: It drives an Age I line at 1024 rpm, which no shaft below ascendant survives. Rebuild the old hall in something stronger.
elysiumalmanac.why.set_the_cage_down: Untuned it sends 4 every 200 to 800 ticks while you are within 16, and stops at 6 of its own nearby. A spawn egg changes what it sends. Everything else is a rune in the hand and a click.
elysiumalmanac.why.settled_places: A hamlet runs to fourteen rooms, a lodge ten, a camp seven, a watchtower eight and mostly stairs. Every one is laid out from its door, so no room is sealed off and none needs mining into.
elysiumalmanac.why.shaft: A shaft carries rotation. Prod any part of a line and it tells you what the whole line is doing.
elysiumalmanac.why.sheet_metal: One ingot, one plate: copper in 80 ticks, iron and gold in 100. A plate is priced as the ingot it was, so rolling is never a way to get more metal, only a shape of it.
elysiumalmanac.why.shortbow_and_sling: At diamond a shortbow does 4 at 2.4 draws a second and costs you nothing to move while drawn. A sling draws 3 a second for 2.5 and is wrong about where the stone goes. Flint and iron to start.
elysiumalmanac.why.sit_and_dine: A stool is four eighths of a block, a chair six, a bench eight. Any wooden one comes upholstered in any of sixteen wools, and costs the bare seat plus exactly one block of wool.
elysiumalmanac.why.six_behaviours: Indifference keeps it awake with nobody near, darkness ignores the light, tethering keeps what it sends, stillness takes their legs, silence their voices, and obedience waits for redstone.
elysiumalmanac.why.sixteen_hands: Sixteen assemblers is as many jobs as one core will run at once. Every one is a machine on the grid, so the power station grows with the factory or the factory slows.
elysiumalmanac.why.sixteen_hundred: Critical at 1,200. At 1,600 the core is gone and takes a radius of eight with it. Four channels settle a full core near 765; three settle it near 984, and wear starts at 800.
elysiumalmanac.why.skillet: Fast and one serving: 200 to 300 ticks. Bacon and eggs for strength, steak and potatoes for resistance, fried rice for haste, grilled fish for water breathing.
elysiumalmanac.why.smelter: The only machine the fourth age adds. Everything else it needs, you already built.
elysiumalmanac.why.solar: Three FE a tick, which is almost nothing. A panel is not a generator — it is the reason a cell is worth building.
elysiumalmanac.why.solar_brass: Three copper and a gold nugget make three ingots: copper warmed with a little gold. Every machine in this set is built of it, and nine keep as a block.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_else: Bind one, and then bind another, and the distance between them costs power rather than time. The price rises with distance and stops rising.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_to_put_thin: The other half of what a room needs. Every shape here can be broken back down, and none of them gives back more than it cost.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_to_sit: Twelve shapes, sixteen materials, and not one of them needs a texture the game did not already have. Start with somewhere to sit down.
elysiumalmanac.why.spallet: A spallet is the smallest thing that hunts you and the one you will meet first. It comes apart when you hit it and the pieces keep coming.
elysiumalmanac.why.split_water: Five water in, ten hydrogen and five oxygen out, for 50 FE. A bottle takes 1,000 mB of oxygen for a suit; a bottle used crouching takes 250 of hydrogen for a motor.
elysiumalmanac.why.stainless: Three steel and a nickel. An alloy of an alloy, which is where a furnace stops being enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.starsteel: An alloy of an alloy of an alloy, and the only thing a tier four casing can be made of. Nothing in the pack is above it, so a starsteel machine is the last one you build.
elysiumalmanac.why.station: Use it in High Orbit with 100 steel and 100 lunite ingots and it builds on your own slot of a 1,024-block grid. From then on a rocket bound for High Orbit lands on your pad.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel: The first thing the age makes for itself, and the gate to the top tier of wire, the diesel engine and the separator.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel_and_invar_casin: A tier one casing is steel and draws 64 FE on the low wire; tier two is invar, 256 on the medium. A machine may be built of anything at or below its rung, never above it.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel_by_fire: Four layers of blast brick, hollow in the middle two. An iron ingot and one coke make steel in 600 ticks with no grid at all. Slower than an arc furnace, and it asks nothing of a wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel_drawer: Four kinds and eight thousand of each. This is what a factory's wall is made of.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel_sheet: The longest roll on the mill at 140 ticks, and every cell, centrifuge and alloy smelter above you is skinned in it. Start a stockpile now and thank yourself later.
elysiumalmanac.why.sting: A sting costs one heart and the bee stays upset for 400 ticks; robbing one upsets its friends six blocks out. A smoker calms every bee within eight for 1,200.
elysiumalmanac.why.stir_it: The hungry one: 12 torque and 32 rpm, which no water wheel reaches ungeared. Gravel to flint, soul soil to soul sand, charcoal to coal, and a poppy to a wither rose in 400 ticks.
elysiumalmanac.why.string_from_flax: Three fibres to a string, so a full row is worth walking down and a single plant is not a string. Spiders still drop one apiece; this is the slower road that is always open.
elysiumalmanac.why.strongbox_and_vault: A strongbox is 45 slots and four fittings; a vault, wrapped in obsidian and iron, 63 and six. With all three pockets a vault holds 117 and pages through them in the game's own chest screen.
elysiumalmanac.why.suit_up: Wool, iron and glass. A full set seals vacuum and radiation, and the chestplate holds 3,000 mB of air: ten minutes outside at 5 a second, then a heart a second until you get in.
elysiumalmanac.why.take_a_cage_apart: Broken without silk touch, a spawner pays for itself: iron, redstone, obsidian, a bottle of experience, and one time in five a rune. With silk touch you keep the whole thing instead.
elysiumalmanac.why.teeth_and_rods: A gear is four ingots cut with teeth and a rod is one drawn out, in steel, invar, stainless and starsteel. The gear is the dear shape, and the one machines want.
elysiumalmanac.why.teeth_that_disagree: Run a line out through a three to one and back into where it began, and one shaft is asked to turn at two speeds. The line jams, nothing turns, and the block that closed the loop says so.
elysiumalmanac.why.terminal: No screen and nothing to search: right-click it holding a thing for a stack of that thing, crouch for one. What comes back is how many steps and how many machine-runs, or why not.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_broad_set: A broad tool swings at 0.55 of the tool it replaces and wins only over a full nine. A paxel is pickaxe, axe and shovel in one slot at 0.75 of each, the price of never switching.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_choir: 120 health, three phases, a red bar. Each phase calls twice its number of Unsworn and quickens, and the room keeps filling between. Ignore the room and by phase three it is the fight.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_commons_kept: Under a shortfall a class is filled whole before the next sees a unit, and two kilns in one class split what is left rather than one dying. Nothing is made or lost on the wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_compass: Pick somewhere and it points at the nearest one. It looks the same distance for everything, however rare, which is why it does not make the server stutter.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_cordon_metals: Cobalt and pearlium dug, seven alloys of two things each: nightgold, relicsteel, slagsteel, biolith, bathysteel, hemalite, nullsteel. The foundry works them into dust and plate.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_crate: Use it on a villager to pick them up and on a block to put them down. Their trades, their level and their restock clock all come with them.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_cuts: Vertical slabs in every material, slabs and stairs in the six the game lacks. Then compact, loft, terrace, skyline and bulk stairs, each proved to climb with no riser over half a block.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_digging_table: Bone and planks make the bench. An iron brush takes 8 ticks a stage where the game's own takes 10, a site has four stages, and no brush may be quicker than 4, so a site is never a pickaxe.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_empires_own: Drones, lictors, adepts and bulwarks: slower, better armoured, and they work as a unit. The adept is weak alone and the reason the others are worse. Kill it first.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_first_tier: Brass is three copper to a zinc, cast iron four iron to a coal dust, electrum gold with silver, constantan copper with nickel. With bronze and invar, the first tier.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_garden_path: A path is a sixteenth deep, a border a quarter, a step three eighths. Sconce 7, post light 10, lamp 13, chandelier 15. And a fence, wall or pane that runs corner to corner, so a field need not be square.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_grave: Everything you were carrying goes into a grave where you fell, sized to what you actually had, and nobody else can open it until you have plainly given up on it.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_half_that_grazes: Twelve animals in four kinds: grazers, foragers, fowl and swimmers. Nothing any of them drops is what any of them is bred with, so a pen is never food out of nothing.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_heavy_answer: The hardest single hit in the pack and the slowest swing behind it. Bring it to something large and leave it at home the rest of the time.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_heavy_shapes: A greatsword does 11 at 0.9 and takes two more with it, a warhammer 13 at 0.75, a longsword 6.5 at 1.9. None of the six is beaten on every axis by another, and the build checks that.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_hollow_lord: It waited a long time for something, and it was not you. Bring the heaviest thing you have and do it in daylight if you can arrange that.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_hundred_and_forty: Twenty-five kinds of land in five reliefs each, crag, flat, hill, scarp and wold, and fifteen caves beneath. The compass looks 12,800 blocks for any of them and rests three seconds.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_long_answer: Slow, enormous, and it takes two more things with it on every swing. The answer to being surrounded, and a poor answer to anything else.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_narrow_answer: Half of what it does goes through armour rather than into it. Against anything in plate it is the best thing here; against anything else it is not.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_old_hall_rewired: Fed 256 FE it drives a line at up to 256 rpm with 96 of torque, and a fifth of what it draws is lost on the way. The first age runs on the second's coal from here on.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_outer_rings: Ashen steppe and coldmarsh, then the rime barrens, frostmere, cinder flats and sulphur springs, where a sulphprime carries 114 health. Walking further out is a decision, never a coin flip.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_plan_first: 256 FE on a medium wire for the planning alone. It holds sixteen jobs in the air and no more, so asking for something dear never empties the warehouse into half-built parts.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_praetor: 150 health, 16 armour, immovable, a purple bar. First a shield a quarter of its health that rebuilds itself; then the shield drops and it returns 35 per cent of every blow you land.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_quick_shapes: At diamond: a sabre does 5 at 2.4 swings a second, a spear 6.5 at 1.2 with a block and a half more reach, an estoc 6 at 1.3 with half of it through armour. Choose by what you are hitting.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_register: Noted brings patrols. Marked brings a three-wave register action, announced ten minutes early so you can spend them. Hunted is five waves ending with the Praetor. Clear one and Suspicion falls.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_saws_kitchen: The saw does every job the kitchen knife does: beef to mince, wheat to dough, milk to butter. It only gives the main thing, and the cream goes on the floor. That is the price of not standing there.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_siege_beast: Three metres of it, and it goes through the wall rather than round it. The hardest thing in the bestiary and the best-paid.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_stalker: You will hear it stop following you, and that is the bad part. The top of the prowlers, and the fastest thing that will ever chase you.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_three_families: A drayhulk will not be knocked back and a carrier burns at dawn. Everything in the dark is one of three families and each wants a different answer.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_vales_own: Twenty-eight things live in the Vale, read as rings around verdant vale where the way in drops you. Everything one ring out is harder than everything in the ring before it.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_yield: Every six world tiers a ripe plant may give one more, on a chance of tier over tier plus ten: a little over a third at six, half at ten, never always. An ore does it every three tiers.
elysiumalmanac.why.things_that_open: In the twenty-two stones and bricks the game has none of, because the eleven wooden sets exist already. Stone wants redstone as iron does, and the tags tell a villager which it may open.
elysiumalmanac.why.things_that_reach: Panes in all thirty-three materials, walls in the twenty-one the game skipped. If A reaches B then B reaches A: proved over every tag, because a join on one side only is a hole in a wall.
elysiumalmanac.why.three_even_shares: Every variant's health, damage and speed add to exactly 3.00: tougher is slower, harder-hitting is frailer. The one ability, checked every 10 ticks, is what makes it a different fight.
elysiumalmanac.why.three_from_one: 2,048 FE on the high wire. Raw iron, copper, gold and uranium come out three for one, debris gives scrap, and nothing anywhere in the pack does better than this.
elysiumalmanac.why.three_ladders_climbed: Prowlers are fast and never alone, brutes hit like a door, wights are patient and burn at noon. Reward is worked out from danger, and the band it sits in includes the game's own zombie.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_arcana: Arcana does not make an enchantment stronger; it decides which are on the table at all, through arcana over arcana plus 25. A sightshelf gives three, an endshelf two. No amount makes a rare one certain.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_arcane_table: The old table, amethyst, diamonds and obsidian. It asks the room for eterna, quanta, arcana and rectification. Three offers at a third, two thirds and all of the eterna, for one, two and three levels.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_armour: Vitality is more of you to lose, ironhide armour that is harder not thicker, bulwark for standing still, nightward for the dark. Kindling sets attackers alight; emberwalk crusts the lava, briefly.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_blades: Venom keeps working after you stop, hoarfrost slows, sundering weakens, siphon heals you. Ambush pays for the unseen hit and charge for the run-up; grave robber takes their gear, scholar more of their experience.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_eterna: A bookshelf gives two eterna and caps the room at fifteen. A hellshelf gives two and a half and lets it reach twenty-five; an archive column three, to forty. You carry a cap of your own: fifty, six more a world tier.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_grand: Four scriptoria, four gold blocks and a diamond block, holding 65,536 pages of each enchantment: sixty-four times the shelf, which is what makes the highest levels something you can bank.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_infusion: A book says what you get and the room how high: eight eterna for each level past the first. Five experience levels and three lapis a level, up to two fifths off for rectification. Quanta does nothing here.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_patience: The game's anvil refuses anything at forty levels. This one charges the real price, and the history still doubles each time up to 63. A book and a clock make the tome that clears that history, once.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_quanta: Quanta is how far either side of the offer the result may land. A deepshelf, sculk and deepslate round a bookshelf, gives three of it: more of the good outcomes and exactly as many more of the bad.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_rectification: The share of quanta's downside that is removed. A keeper's shelf gives twelve per cent and caps the room at forty; with enough of them an uncertain table keeps all its upside and none of its risk.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_room: A room built for eterna and one built for arcana are different rooms, and the table holds the lesser of the room's cap and yours. Twenty-four shelves chosen, not counted.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_scriptorium: File a book and it becomes pages of that enchantment: two to the level less one. A copy costs twice what it is worth, so four books buy the level above. A shelf holds 1,024 pages of each.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_three_more: On an anvil, each once. Scrapping takes every enchantment off so a table looks again; transcription moves them all onto a book and spends the item; concentration narrows a mixed book to its best line.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_tools: Prospector takes more experience out of the same stone; long arm reaches half a block further a level. Volley looses more arrows, steady aim one true one, thrift keeps some, maelstrom a harder riptide.
elysiumalmanac.why.tome_tower: Somewhere in the Overworld a tower of tomes stands with a chest in it: tomes, enchanted books, lapis, paper and bottles of experience. Cheaper than crafting them, if you can find one.
elysiumalmanac.why.tools_and_armour_regr: One hammer to a kind of gear and never two: the toolsmith's for tools, the armourer's for armour and shields. The best grade is never worth a step up the ladder, so it never replaces one.
elysiumalmanac.why.top_of_the_fuels: Creosote through the refinery again: 48,000 ticks of burn. Only this engine takes it, at 256 rpm free and 72 torque, faster than brass survives, so keep it loaded or lose the line.
elysiumalmanac.why.top_of_the_ladder: The top rung: 17 added damage, 5,248 uses, enchantability 20. Each rung above the game's own does 15 per cent more than the one below, which is more than any reforge can give.
elysiumalmanac.why.totems_set_down: A growth totem bone-meals within 6 every 200 ticks; a radiance totem works within 12 every 400. A placed totem works for ever for nothing, so what one may do in a minute is capped at six.
elysiumalmanac.why.totems_spent: A torrent totem throws you the way you are looking; a soul totem takes 4 from the nearest thing within 8 and gives it to you. Used once and gone, two seconds before another will answer.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_anchor: The foot of a space elevator: iron blocks, chain and a redstone block. Placing it or using it reads the column above and says where it stops, how far short it is, or what roofs it over.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_charter: Each world has one. Local materials are worked a quarter faster and carried ones a third slower; each hazard is a daily burden on the people, cut by sealing but never below a fifth.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_command: Bare, it reports the town you stand in: charter, what is underfoot, what a day's work is worth. People names the five most miserable; natural lists self-founded towns, nearest first.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_counterweight: Iron blocks round an anvil, at the very top, with nothing between it and the sky. Roof it over and you have built a very tall warehouse.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_exchange: A town keeps sixty-four of everything and sells the rest to buy what it lacks, at most 128 a day. Each deal is a point of Suspicion, five at most. A lifeline, priced like one.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_found: Found one with MineColonies' town hall, or stand in a self-founded town and /elysium colony claim it. Either is two Suspicion of floor a citizen up to sixty, and raiders at your tier.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_legs: Four legs on the diagonals, twelve out at the deck and three out by 36 up, bent so the top stands nearly straight. Each standing leg ships sixty-four more a day. Collars are lit.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_relief: For its first hundred days a town is supplied free, up to sixty-four stacks a day. A town that finishes nothing for four days is stuck, whatever the reason, and the remedy escalates.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_ruins: Every fifty-six chunks a ruin marker raises one building as it fell: floors intact, walls thinning as they rise, roofs mostly gone, wood rotted first. There is a chest of what was left.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_spaceport: 256 items a day at eighty blocks, four more for every block above. It exports the surplus, freights from any colony with what you lack, then imports, all before the exchange is tried.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_survey: The world plants a survey stake every forty chunks, none within 24 of spawn. The first time anybody comes near, it founds a town and is gone; a level-N building takes N days.
elysiumalmanac.why.town_tether: Four to a recipe of iron and chain, and eighty unbroken is the least that is an elevator rather than a mast. Cut it anywhere and the port stops, which is why it is worth defending.
elysiumalmanac.why.trading_station: Crate a villager into a station and it trades once every three seconds from what it is given. Never better value than a hand, and its restock clock travels in the crate, so moving it is not a new day.
elysiumalmanac.why.transformer: The one block allowed two voltages on it. Everywhere else, the higher one destroys the lower.
elysiumalmanac.why.transmuter: Dissolve something and you get most of its worth back as motes; spend motes and you get back anything you have dissolved before. A round trip always loses a tenth, so there is no loop in it worth riding.
elysiumalmanac.why.trophies: Every species has a bucket and a mount, because a mount for a hundred and four of a hundred and five fish is a hole exactly one player finds, and they find it holding the fish.
elysiumalmanac.why.truck: A cart, a motor and steel plate: 11 blocks a second on a road, 27 slots, two seats, and it drinks 0.11 a block. A full load costs a third of the speed and adds a third to the thirst.
elysiumalmanac.why.turbine: A firebox and a boiler. It only burns when something on the grid actually wants the power.
elysiumalmanac.why.turn_a_corner: The only way power goes round a corner. It changes no speed, reverses whatever it turns, and costs one gear stage like anything else with teeth in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.two_ends_of_a_pool: Use a link holding an item and it joins that item's channel; two links on one channel share one pool at any distance. Four devices of draw each, the dearest thing a network can carry.
elysiumalmanac.why.two_in_one_out: Two metals in given counts, one alloy out. No step in the chain may come out worth more than went into it, and no metal is ever made, however far down, out of itself.
elysiumalmanac.why.two_lines_one_wall: A wire and a dye in the grid make a dyed wire. Runs join when either is plain or both share a colour, so two grids can pass side by side through one wall and never meet.
elysiumalmanac.why.two_more_fittings: A hopper pot drops its harvest into whatever is beneath it, so a room of them wants nothing from you but light. A waxed pot grows at exactly the speed a plain one does.
elysiumalmanac.why.upgrades: One of each kind to a housing. Capacity adds twelve bees, speed is 1.5 times, flowering counts the flowers as planted, collection takes the combs. An advanced apiary has four slots.
elysiumalmanac.why.varied_diet: The bonus is an attribute rather than a heal: it survives death, relog and a change of world, and is reset to what the rules say each tick, so nobody ends up with ninety hearts and no idea why.
elysiumalmanac.why.verdigris: Copper and a moss block make two verdigris: copper given time and damp, then stopped there. On copper it is panelling aged on purpose; on terracotta it is mosaic tile, four to a craft.
elysiumalmanac.why.void_silt: The top of the soil ladder at 1.9, and the only soil that grows chorus, ender bloom, kelp and mushrooms all at once. It costs end stone, which is why it comes last.
elysiumalmanac.why.void_steel: Stainless and uranium: the third age's metal in the fourth age's pot. With starsteel it is the top tier, and nothing in the chain may be made of anything above it.
elysiumalmanac.why.watch_the_work: A pane of glass on the bus that says what the network is making and what it waits on. One device of draw, and the cheapest way to learn why the core has gone quiet.
elysiumalmanac.why.water_wheel: A crank stops when you walk away. A water wheel does not, and that is the whole of the first age's lesson.
elysiumalmanac.why.waygate_built: Five by five: fifteen frames of obsidian, cryonite and steel, the anchor bottom centre and the middle clear. A gate reaches only another gate, so the first trip anywhere is still a rocket.
elysiumalmanac.why.waygate_found: Standing rings on pale brick turn up at home, on the moon and on both planets. Use the anchor at the bottom and it lists every finished gate. Going is free; there is no fuel and no toll.
elysiumalmanac.why.waystone: Bind two and you can jump between them for a price the grid pays. An unwired stone fills from nothing, so the short way home costs a minute; wire it and the minute goes away.
elysiumalmanac.why.weaponsmiths_hammer: Every weapon and bow is graded when first made or picked up, and this hammer rolls it again. Dull and unwieldy are nearly half the table; fabled is one in 116 and costs 12 levels to leave.
elysiumalmanac.why.wear_and_plate: Above 800 degrees a core wears, and the last few hundred cost far more than the first. At full wear it stops. Each steel plate you give it takes a quarter of the wear off.
elysiumalmanac.why.welcome: Everything in this pack hangs off four ages of machinery. You are at the bottom of the first one, and it needs no power.
elysiumalmanac.why.what_else_is_buried: A fossil site gives up chiseled bone one time in six and an echo shard one in twenty. Every pool keeps its rarest find above one in two hundred, because rarer than that is simply absent.
elysiumalmanac.why.what_it_turned_out_to: Penetrating strike puts 12 per cent of a blow through armour a level, to three; soaring winds starts an elytra flight; tunneling takes more blocks. Hold it with the gear in the other hand.
elysiumalmanac.why.what_the_grid_says: Any wire reports its grid: supply, demand, share. Copper loses 0.4 per cent a block, and two rolling mills on one turbine get 0.62 each and run slower rather than stop.
elysiumalmanac.why.what_the_rock_held: Stainless casing, 1,024 FE on the high wire: one raw ore to three ingots in 200 ticks, and three nuggets of the metal the rock held beside it. Iron gives up nickel; copper, gold.
elysiumalmanac.why.white_stone: Marble, limestone and alabaster seam the overworld. Polish four for four, then cut slab, stairs and wall. Ring one in eight ingots for an edged block, or set four round one for filigree.
elysiumalmanac.why.wild_crops: Eight crops, each generating untended somewhere: onion and barley in plains, garlic in forest, tomato in savanna, chili in desert, ginger in jungle, rice in swamp water.
elysiumalmanac.why.wild_downbloom: The second wild plant, found the same way and just as sparse. Downbloom gives tuft rather than fibre, and tuft is softer stuff: four to a string instead of three, and it bales.
elysiumalmanac.why.wild_loomflax: Twelve plants to a patch and two tries a chunk, so you find one in an afternoon and never farm the wild ones. A wild plant gives two seeds: enough to start, not enough to skip planting.
elysiumalmanac.why.wind_it_up: One turn drives the line for 100 ticks and then it runs down. Free, a crank turns 32 rpm; hang a millstone on it and it settles at 16. Enough to grind a stack while you stand there.
elysiumalmanac.why.worm_farm: Feed it a fish and it makes the bait for that fish's family, one every 1,200 ticks, until it holds sixteen. Seventy-two an hour at most: a convenience, not a switch.
elysiumalmanac.why.worn_path: Two gravel and two dirt make four. A path gives a vehicle 72% of its road speed at 1.15 times the fuel, and so does a trodden dirt path. Open ground gives half, rough ground under a third.
elysiumalmanac.why.worth_the_trouble: The second rung of all three ladders. Every one of them is worth more than the thing below it, and that is a promise this pack actually checks.
elysiumalmanac.why.yellow_ore: Raw uranium and raw uraninite both come out of a furnace as a uranium ingot, in 200 ticks or 100 blasted. The centrifuge wants the ingot; the enricher gets more out of the raw ore.
elysiumalmanac.why.your_own_roll: A chest in a dungeon gives every player their own loot, and the same player the same loot every time. The roll is worked out from you and the chest, so closing it is not a reroll.
